review_reference: Owner decision 25 (D-Eminence, 2026-11-01, in chat): "all recommended except D5" on the Akos handover backend plan, items 3b and 4 (Akos plan step 4, migration 0114, released as 0122; D6: no drug picture until the price list; D9: the pharmacist confirms the quantity)
evidence: 0122 (prescription strength, form, duration, quantity and priority for the pharmacy) is backward compatible, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). Review reference: owner decision 25 of 2026-11-01 (D-Eminence, in chat), "all recommended except D5", on the Akos handover backend plan, items 3b and 4 (Akos plan step 4; D6: no drug picture until the price list; D9: the quantity to dispense is the prescriber's suggestion, the pharmacist confirms it and nothing compares the two). NUMBER AND ORDER: the plan's 0107 was numbered 0114 (coordinator's numbering of 3 Nov 2026) and released jointly with 0113; by the coordinator's release order of 11 Nov 2026 (0117 to 0122 fixed in that order) it is 0122 and ships on its own after 0121 (the own-work patient cards, #160, formerly 0113), which has its own declaration. This declaration therefore lists only 0122 and runtime-grants.sql, and assumes production has applied 0121; if it has not, the release stops with EXACT_SCHEMA_CHANGE_DECLARATION_REQUIRED (or the declaration must be widened to 0121, 0122 and runtime-grants.sql). 0122 uses nothing 0121 adds and relies on no body 0121 creates; runtime-grants.sql here holds 0121's block and then 0122's (EXECUTE on the Pharmacy details reader). 0112-0120 belong to other work and are not on this branch. WHAT CHANGES. ehr.prescriptions gains seven nullable columns without default, so no rewrite and every existing row reads null: priority, medication_strength, medication_dose_form, duration_value integer, duration_unit, quantity_to_dispense numeric(12,4) and quantity_unit (the others text), and one CHECK, prescriptions_dispensing_details_ck, added NOT VALID and then validated, so the table is scanned once: priority routine, urgent, asap or stat; medication_strength and quantity_unit not blank and at most 80 characters; medication_dose_form tablet, capsule, liquid, injection, cream, inhaler, drops or other; duration_value 1-3650 and duration_unit day, week or month, both or neither; quantity_to_dispense above 0 and quantity_unit, both or neither (one CHECK for the seven columns, not one per rule, because each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT scans the whole table under the lock; the EHR API checks each rule by name before it writes). One new function, pharmacy.work_item_prescription_details(uuid[]) (md5 e6013d732354a56794ad8ec7f2bbaf0c), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name qualified), owned by pharmacy.work_items' owner, no migration number in its body. For each given work item that is own work (order_route_id null) at the session's facility, whose member holds pharmacy.work-item.read there (auth.membership_has_permission) and passes identity.has_active_consent_grant(patient, subject, membership, facility, 'read_records', the session's purpose), the own-row branch of the work items' read policy (so an emergency session with an active break-glass grant is included, and a revoked, expired or held grant, a deny directive, an inactive membership or a disabled account gives no row), it answers the seven values of the prescription version Pharmacy accepted, read from that version's snapshot in ehr.record_versions (resource_type 'prescriptions', resource_id the prescription id, version_no the accepted version, naming the work item's patient, facility and encounter), so they stay those of the accepted version after the prescription changes. The work item's keys are turned into text in a materialized CTE before the join, so the join compares text with text (texteq is leakproof) and uses the snapshot key (resource_type, resource_id, version_no) under the forced read policy, which then runs once per work item; a join on the uuid cast to text inside it (uuid_out is not leakproof) cannot be an index condition below the policy, which then ran on every prescription snapshot of the item's patient or facility. At most 200 ids, else 22023 WORK_ITEM_PRESCRIPTION_DETAILS_INVALID. The snapshot path was decided by test: ehr.record_versions' only read policy is ehr.context_allows(patient_id, facility_id, 'read_records'), the same facility-and-consent test for an own row, and under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner the suite reads every expected value through it. Nothing is copied into pharmacy.work_items: pharmacy.validate_work_item (0100, e2411539ee8c95a02dad46c03e24db05), pharmacy.validate_dispensing (0101, 17f7e8897bd2ab240332e4d2c9f757b7), ehr.send_order_route (0098, 4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c), ehr.sync_order_routes_on_order_change (0086, 8ce6b42450cc06fc02fec8d1cf63af41) and ehr.capture_record_version (0004, 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702) are untouched and checked before and after. No policy, trigger, index, role or other function changes; no existing row is touched. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0122 block: EXECUTE to hid_pharmacy_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, revoked from PUBLIC; the migration grants exactly the same; the EHR runtime's privileges on ehr.prescriptions are table-wide and cover the new columns. SERVICES: each behind PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED, new in ehr-api and in pharmacy-api, off by default (the infrastructure sets no value). Off, ehr-api validates the create body against today's CreatePrescriptionDto with the options main.ts installs (now one shared factory), so a new field answers today's 400 VALIDATION_FAILED word for word (jest, over HTTP, against a route declared as before), no statement names the new columns and no answer or list carries a new key; pharmacy-api sends no new statement and answers exactly as before (jest). On, POST .../prescriptions takes the seven as optional, create-only fields (pairs enforced: 400 DURATION_INCOMPLETE or QUANTITY_INCOMPLETE), every prescription answer echoes the ones set, the list says dispensingDetails: true, and a body without them keeps its Idempotency-Key digest (absent DTO fields are own undefined properties, which the digest prints, so the new ones are left out when absent and a retry across the deploy replays); pharmacy-api adds priority, medication.strength, medication.doseForm, duration (else the whole days from the work item's own start date to its end date, when both are set) and quantityToDispense with quantityUnit to own rows of the work list and of a work item, read in a savepoint (a failure leaves out the prescriber's values; the duration from the work item's own dates stays); route-backed rows and the acceptance answer are unchanged and no audit row is added. Today's images on the new schema answer as before: every writer and reader of ehr.prescriptions names its columns, and the bodies that read the row into ehr.prescriptions%ROWTYPE re-resolve after ADD COLUMN, also in a pooled connection that ran them before (proved: one psql session ran the pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source and order-routes-send suites on 0103 + 0113, the runner applied 0114 (now 0122) from another connection, and the same session ran them and the 0122 suite again, all passing; the 0122 suite also adds a further column in its own session and accepts, dispenses and reads again). Switch the ehr-api setting on only after 0122 is applied, and off before restoring ehr-api's database to a point before 0122 or pointing ehr-api at a database without it: while it is on without the seven columns every prescription statement names them and fails (42703), so every prescription route of ehr-api answers 500; pharmacy-api only leaves the prescriber's values out (savepoint). Cost while the pharmacy-api setting is on: each list load calls the reader once for its own rows (at most 200), a statement of its own, under pharmacy-api's 15 s statement limit; under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner each row pays the work items' read policy, the same consent test again and the snapshot table's read policy, once each (pg_stat_user_functions: 200 snapshot-policy calls for 200 items): 1.0-1.7 s for 200 own rows, against 0.4-0.7 s for reading the same rows under row-level security, with 1, 5, 20 or 50 prescription snapshots per patient and with 300,000 other snapshots at the facility (fictional data, a shared 4-CPU machine). The first draft's join on the uuid cast to text took 3.5 s with 5 and 8.8 s with 20 snapshots per patient (4,000 snapshot-policy calls for 200 items), and stopped at the 15 s limit with 1 per patient beside 100,000 other prescription snapshots, so the details would have been dropped; the answers of both bodies were identical wherever both finished. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0103 applied (0103's identity.organization_application_admin_account body md5 186eb4ca420749b8bdb324bdc843bc50 the marker, and the three tables used); not applied yet (the function does not exist); none of the seven columns or the CHECK name on ehr.prescriptions; md5 of ehr.capture_record_version, identity.has_active_consent_grant 8b12ce866ee75cce411a2721795ffb92, identity.has_active_membership bb52953ef1cd08527db61230a671859e, auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6, platform.current_actor_subject cf14c2d4a16d44a79ea9dbef9dc79c2b, current_facility_id c4a7c2989e83d9cedbf1f7b785a5aaed, current_membership_id 641989704fea95f885fbc38c6feb5aa5, current_purpose_of_use 74f7f2ea17dbbe825f7cfe543ad3e83f, pharmacy.work_item_allows b710e0c6b66ce87c8c4a059ad435b774, ehr.order_route_allows b80c2df6c380f7c7e20d166da94e56d2, ehr.context_allows 75016690184a80bd246c365b4d108082 and the four untouched bodies above; the language, SECURITY DEFINER, volatility, result and search_path of eight of them (pharmacy.work_item_allows' body is byte-identical to Lab's, so its search_path tells them apart); the three triggers on ehr.prescriptions (exact definitions, enabled, no other); pharmacy_work_items_read and record_versions_read as the only SELECT policies of their tables, by table and name; work_items_route_facility_ck; record_versions' UNIQUE (resource_type, resource_id, version_no); forced row-level security on pharmacy.work_items and ehr.record_versions; the types and NOT NULLs of the 18 columns read; the applier is ehr.prescriptions' and pharmacy.work_items' owner or a member that inherits each and may SET ROLE to it, and may create in schema pharmacy; that function owner may create in and use pharmacy, use ehr, identity, auth and platform, read pharmacy.work_items and ehr.record_versions and execute the eight functions the body and the two read policies call. Negative copies on a 0103 + 0113 base (before the renumber, as 0114), each run in one transaction, all 25 stopped with nothing applied (no function, no column): the marker renamed (0001-0103 must be applied first); the bodies of the 0100 guard, the snapshot writer, ehr.context_allows and platform.current_facility_id changed, and ehr.sync_order_routes_on_order_change renamed (md5 none (missing)); pharmacy.work_item_allows' search_path changed; ehr.context_allows and identity.has_active_consent_grant made SECURITY INVOKER; an extra SELECT policy and an extra FOR ALL policy on ehr.record_versions, record_versions_read changed, a role policy on pharmacy.work_items; FORCE lifted on ehr.record_versions, row-level security off on pharmacy.work_items; prescriptions_versioned disabled or set to replica, an extra trigger on ehr.prescriptions; the snapshot key dropped, work_items_route_facility_ck dropped; a priority column already there, the CHECK name already used; pharmacy.work_items.source_encounter_id made nullable (all 55000); pharmacy.work_items owned by a role without the privileges (42501 listing each), a stranger with USAGE on every schema (42501, not the owner and may not act as it); a second apply answers 0122: already applied. LOCKS, measured with pg_locks before commit on a 0103 + 0113 copy (as 0114): ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.prescriptions held to commit (and VALIDATE's SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE inside it), unchanged by the review fixes; ACCESS SHARE on schema pharmacy, the language plpgsql and the two granted roles; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the new function; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the session's own temporary schema; no other application table lock held to commit. The table lock is taken NOWAIT and retried every 100 ms for at most 5 s: behind a Pharmacy acceptance held open through pharmacy-api's runtime and INSERT (0100's FOR SHARE on its prescription) the runner's dry run stopped after 5.2-5.3 s with "0122: ehr.prescriptions stayed busy for 5 seconds; run the release again at a quieter time", 0122 still pending, while another session's read of ehr.prescriptions took 70-81 ms (measured again after the review fixes). Behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on pharmacy.work_items or ehr.record_versions the runner stopped after its 5 s lock timeout (5.2 s), nothing applied; behind ROW EXCLUSIVE on either, or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.patients, it applied at once. Each migration runs in one transaction, so ADD COLUMN's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is still held while VALIDATE scans and NOT VALID then VALIDATE does not shorten the lock here; it is kept as the rule for CHECKs on existing tables, with the rules in one CHECK so that the table is scanned once: ADD COLUMN with the NOT VALID CHECK took 2-8 ms and the one validation 73 ms for 200,000 prescriptions and 0.48 s for 1,000,000 (synthetic tables; nine separate CHECKs took 0.43 s and 3.05 s there), during which EHR prescription reads and writes and Pharmacy acceptances and dispensings wait. Apply time 18-56 ms (execution_ms) on the test databases. PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 before the renumber, as 0114 on 0103 + 0113: the new suite fails on 0113 and on 0103; a database built by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (0001-0103 and 0113 applied as it): 0114 applied by a member login of that owner (INHERIT and SET; the function then belongs to the owner), bootstrap and verification passed, and the new suite and the work-item-patient-cards, pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source, order-routes-receive, order-routes-privileges and order-routes-send suites passed with that owner. 31 of 33 mutants killed by the suite with its md5 pin taken out (no own-row filter, no consent test, write consent, direct-care only, no permission check, the Lab permission, no 200 limit, a null list accepted, a snapshot of any patient, of any facility, of any encounter or at any version, the singular resource type 'prescription', the live row instead of the snapshot, the strength from the medicine's name, the quantity unit from the duration unit, PUBLIC or EHR runtime EXECUTE, and in the CHECK: no duration pair, no quantity pair, priority without asap, any dose form, any duration unit, a strength or a quantity unit of 81, a blank strength or quantity unit, a quantity of 0, a duration of 0 or of 3651, the CHECK left NOT VALID); the two survivors are the session-facility filter dropped, which the consent test already implies (a membership belongs to one facility), kept as defence in depth, and the CTE without MATERIALIZED, which answers the same and differs only in cost, and which the md5 pins in the file's post-check and in the suite stop. ehr-api jest 216 (the prescriptions, shared, config, common and offline files, with a test that an idempotent replay answers exactly as the create; dropping the replay's projection fails it) and tsc, pharmacy-api jest 244 and tsc, api-client tsc passed. ROLLBACK: 0122 has no down migration. To withdraw the feature, set PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED=false in ehr-api and pharmacy-api; the columns, any values written and the function stay and nothing reads them. Do not drop the function: 0122 stays recorded, so the runner does not re-create it, and runtime-grants.sql's 0122 block would then stop db:bootstrap (proved on a copy: after the drop the plan answered 0 pending and db:bootstrap failed on the missing function). SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/prescription-dispensing-details.integration.sql: structure (body by md5, attributes, owner, EXECUTE exactly for the Pharmacy runtime, its API login and the schema test runtime; the columns and the validated CHECK; the untouched bodies); 36 CHECK cases through the EHR API's INSERT (each value set and range, both pairs, blank and long texts, numeric overflow) and today's INSERT leaving all seven null; the snapshot carries them; acceptances through pharmacy-api's INSERT under 0100's guard and a dispensing under 0101's pass; a pharmacist gets exactly the accepted version's values for its own rows, seven nulls for a prescription without them and for one written before 0122, and still the accepted version's after the EHR changes the prescription twice (while 0101 refuses its dispensing); no row for a route-backed work item (also one naming this facility's own prescription), another facility's own work, a patient without a grant, a snapshot of another patient, facility or encounter or at a version that has none, a member with consent but without the read permission, a session at another facility, without a membership, with an unknown subject, without a purpose, under emergency without a break-glass grant or with another member's membership, a revoked or expired grant, a deny directive, a disabled account or a held membership; a malformed facility setting refused 22023; the EHR and Lab runtimes refused 42501; a doctor with consent and the read permission gets its row; emergency: a break-glass grant gets exactly its readable rows, also under a deny directive, nothing under direct care; 200 ids read, 201 (also as a 2 x 101 array) and null refused 22023, an empty list answers nothing; the reads write no audit or snapshot row; after a further ADD COLUMN in the same session a prescription, its acceptance, its dispensing and its details still pass. Fictional data only.
